rationale: All 8 acceptance criteria pass and the implementation is correct for the intended inputs. One major patch finding: the truthiness guard `if _raw_extra else None` before `.items()` does not protect against a truthy non-dict type (e.g. a list returned by a misbehaving enterprise IDP plugin); the resulting AttributeError is silently absorbed by the broad except-Exception handler in authenticate() and returned as a 401, masking the real cause. Two deferred design notes (not blocking): `sub` is intentionally in the denylist per spec — noted for future reference if a deployment needs it forwarded; JWT values are inherently JSON-serializable by definition so the dict[str,Any] annotation is acceptable. Three findings dismissed as incorrect (test isolation — lazy imports ARE inside the patch.dict scope; denylist test — test_extra_attributes_denylist_strips_jwt_metadata exists; User.extra_attributes not excluded — intentional per AC2).

findings.problem: The guard `if _raw_extra else None` before `_raw_extra.items()` protects only against falsy values (None, empty dict), not against truthy non-dict types such as a list or string returned by a misbehaving enterprise IDP plugin.
findings.impact: Any truthy non-dict value raises AttributeError inside authenticate(), which is caught by the broad `except Exception` handler at line 125 and returned as a 401 'Authentication failed' — masking the real root cause and making the bug extremely hard to diagnose in production. No test covers this input class.
findings.recommendation: Replace `if _raw_extra else None` with `if isinstance(_raw_extra, dict) else None`; add a logger.warning (or logger.error) for the non-dict case at the authentication boundary so the failure surface is visible rather than absorbed.
